raw_response:
I am getting older and there is only me at home, so this year I will not spread myself too thin. I will keep most of the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest way here, and keep a smaller piece in cotton for cash. I do not read those technical tables, I look at what worked before and what the farmers around me are doing. Wheat and maize are familiar, and with the well I can still protect them if spring is dry, but water and fertilizer cost money, so I will not push too hard. For cotton, I will keep it on the land that usually suits it, but not too much, because picking takes labor and I am alone.

For wheat, I will sow on time in October on 12 mu, use improved local seed, put most fertilizer as base and then one topdressing at jointing. I would rather spend a bit more on wheat fertilizer than see the leaves turn yellow and lose yield. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant summer maize right away on the same 12 mu. The turnaround is short, so I will keep tillage simple and hire machine help if needed. For cotton, I will plant 8 mu in April, use moderate fertilizer, irrigate when it is dry, and spray only when insects or weeds really show up. This way I keep some grain, some cash crop, and I do not take on more work than I can handle alone.
